assumptions.servo_source: Official Feetech FS90MG drawing p.5, edition A/0, 2021-04-30, ±0.1 mm. File copied to datasheets/FS90MG.pdf.
assumptions.horn: ASSUMED typical 2.0 mm disc + 4-arm star, Ø24. Not on the drawing. p.6 says No Accessories.
assumptions.spline_teeth: Drawing and 6-9 say 20T/Ø4.7; product pages say 21T. Measure on arrival.
assumptions.arm_servos: 2× FS90MG, one per arm, spline along x at y=13 z=60, direct drive on the horn (v4).
assumptions.speaker: Adafruit 3351 Mono Enclosed 3W 4Ω, 70×30×17, Core A$8.95
assumptions.fastener_scheme: M2.5 clearance 2.8 / pilot 2.1 (front=clearance, back=pilot). Servo self-tap pilots 1.7. Retainer M2 clearance 2.3 / pilot 1.7.
assumptions.running_fit: Journal radial and blade side 0.35 mm (tight end of 0.35–0.4 FDM). Axial washer gap 0.30 mm. Retainer play 0.35 mm.

rows.interface: Head pan joint (motorised yaw, FS90MG in the collar)
rows.parts: yaw_collar, yaw_coupler, head_back, head_front, dummy_servo_yaw, dummy_horn_yaw
rows.measured: Pan servo is the v3 collar FS90MG (unchanged): horn → coupler blade → slot in head_back. Software clamp ±42° (84° of the 180° servo travel), hard stop ≈ ±47°. Sweep: 1017 poses, rigid overlaps in travel = 0; first yaw stop contact {'yaw': 47.0, 'armL': -20.0, 'armR': -20.0, 'a': 'yaw_collar', 'b': 'head_back', 'vol_mm3': 0.619, 'compliant': ''}.
rows.fix: Tilt was not added: a nod yoke plus a 4th FS90MG does not fit cleanly in the 64 mm head beside the camera and FPC loop.

rows.interface: Neck cable path (pan servo + camera FPC)
rows.measured: The pan servo is fixed in the torso-side collar, so its 3-wire lead never crosses the moving joint: it drops straight down beside the servo body into the torso. Only the camera FPC crosses the neck: floor slot (x=14) → Ø34 collar bore → r=14 U-bend loop bay in the head (π·14 ≈ 44 mm slack for ±42°). Floor slot probe width 30.2 mm (design 2.5). Collar bore Ø34 stays open above the boss for service.
rows.fix: Do not twist the FPC around the yaw axis; let it roll in the U-bend.

rows.measured: Arm angle 0 = straight forward, + = up. Software clamp −55°..+70° (125° of the 180° servo travel; −55° keeps the paw off the desk).
